newsitem.title: USA: CME March lumber rises $10 limit in late trading.
newsitem.headline: CME March lumber rises $10 limit in late trading.

text.p: CME March lumber futures rose the $10 per tbf daily limit in late trading, and May lumber was sharply higher in reaction to firm cash prices and perception that the U.S. housing market remains strong, analysts said.

The U.S. Commerce Department early Wednesday reported a 12.2 percent drop in U.S. housing starts in December, which exceeded analysts' estimates. However, analysts said much of the decline came in the western U.S. where flooding was severe.
"It was purely regional and largely weather-related," said one analyst.
Outside of the flooded areas, traders and analysts said the housing market appeared strong.
At 1237 CST, lumber was up $10.00 to $4.10, with March up the limit at $427.30 and May up $7.70 at $393.00.
